thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: KV-cache continuous-batching regression detected in prod cluster us-west-2. Metric spikes: kv_evictions +250%, request tail latency 95p -> 1.3s, overall token throughput down ~18% for affected shard set. Possible cause: recent microbatch autotune change (rollout v3) interacting with high-seq-length traffic from a few tenants. Root thread_ts=2443211111

alex: I'm on it, seeing the same alarms. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/team/kv-cache/seqlen-amplification (tl;dr: per-tenant seqlen 10->300 spikes causing batch expansion + cache churn)

maya: Noted customer impact. Support flagged a major customer "NimbusCorp" with 40% increased error rate on their embedding endpoints. Support ticket #INC-4229.

tomas: Can we pin which feature flag rollout touched batch sizing? I think it was `batch.autotune.v3` last night at 02:12 UTC.

alex: Confirmed: `ffctl get batch.autotune` shows v3 active in prod across 6 shards. Canary was supposed to be 10% but rollout reached ~60% due to orchestration bug.

sre-ivy: Repro on staging: load profile with many long sequences triggers kv paging; continuous batching expands batches aggressively and evicts prefixes. Repro steps attached as paste: ```bash
# quick repro (staging)
python tools/load_gen.py --model elm --seq-len 250 --rps 80 --duration 600
```

maya: Immediate mitigation plan? We should prioritize restoring latency for affected tenants first. Options: 1) Flip feature flag back to v2, 2) Apply per-customer batch cap override for NimbusCorp, 3) Hotpatch runtime to enforce max_batch_size=64.

alex: I'm leaning to do a per-customer override for NimbusCorp + throttled rollback of autotune v3. That minimizes blast radius and buys SRE time. I'll prepare the override.

tomas: Agree. How to apply override quickly? We have `custctl` for per-tenant config. Use: `custctl set-config NimbusCorp batch.max_batch_size=48 kv.prefetch=false --env prod`

alex: On it. Running: `custctl set-config NimbusCorp batch.max_batch_size=48 kv.prefetch=false --env prod --reason "live mitigation seqlen spike"`

deploy-bot: custctl: change accepted for tenant NimbusCorp. Change id: CUSTCFG-8912. Propagating to edge in 6s.

sre-ivy: Watching metrics, will report within 2 mins.

support-linda: Notified NimbusCorp CSM and engineering contact (j.park). They've pushed a partial queue reduction on their side but want us to keep them updated.

(3m later)

sre-ivy: Early signal: kv_evictions decreased 12% for the target shard, tail latency for NimbusCorp 95p dropped from 1.3s -> 420ms. Good sign but not fully recovered.

alex: Next: schedule rollback of batch.autotune.v3 to v2 gradationally. I propose: set rollout to 20% immediately, watch 5m, then 0% if stable. Command: `ffctl set batch.autotune=v2 --rollout 20% --env prod --by shard`

tomas: Make sure the shard-scoped rollout targets low-traffic shards first. We don't want to create token backlog from a sudden shrink. Use `--exclude region=ap-south` (that's high variance).

alex: Executing: `ffctl set batch.autotune=v2 --rollout 20% --scope shard:us-west-2-a --env prod --reason "mitigation after seqlen amp"`

deploy-bot: feature-flag change queued: FF-CHANGE-3344. Target scope: shard:us-west-2-a. Estimated propagation 90s.

(4m later)

sre-ivy: Metrics look healthier on the shard where we applied per-tenant override and the 20% rollback. Global kv_evictions trending down 18% in last 5m. No new customer errors reported so far.

maya: Should we start a canary for a runtime hotpatch (enforce `max_batch_size=64` globally) or keep firefighting with flags and per-tenant overrides? Hotpatch has higher risk.

alex: I think avoid global hotpatch for now. Use targeted per-tenant and shard-level flag rollbacks while we root cause. Hotpatch if rollback doesn't stabilize within 30m.

support-linda: NimbusCorp says latency improved but still seeing retries at the SDK layer; asked for ETA on full recovery. I'll let them know we're in mitigation and monitoring.

tomas: For postmortem we need to capture: why orchestrator allowed 60% rollout instead of 10%, and why autotune triggers expansion under high seqlen rather than capping. Also test coverage gap for mixed seqlen traffic.

alex: Action items:
- alex: monitor cust metrics + complete full rollback schedule if stable (target 0% rollout if no regression in 15m).
- maya: own customer comms and triage for NimbusCorp.
- tomas: reproduce locally and prepare PR to add a safety cap to autotune (hard cap max_batch_size=128) + add unit/integration tests for mixed seqlen workloads.
- sre-ivy: keep an eye on kv_evictions, contention and memory pressure alerts.
- support-linda: update NimbusCorp; keep support ticket open.

sre-ivy: Also enabling enhanced tracing for affected shards to collect sampling traces: `tracectl enable -s us-west-2-a --rate 0.05 --span kv:batch`

deploy-bot: tracectl: sampling enabled on us-west-2-a. Trace ID batch-sample-5591.

(15m later)

sre-ivy: Stable signals for 12 consecutive minutes. Rollback the rest of rollout? alex?

alex: Rolling down remaining rollout to 0% across other affected shards with staggered schedule to avoid backlog: `ffctl set batch.autotune=v2 --rollout 0% --stagger 60s --env prod --reason "rollback after mitigation"`

deploy-bot: FF-CHANGE-3344: rollback in progress. ETA 6m.

(20m later)

sre-ivy: All affected shards show kv_evictions back to baseline, 95p latency near normal. NimbusCorp error rate cleared. Marking incident as mitigated for now.

maya: Good. I'll prepare first incident summary for CSM and NimbusCorp with timeline and ask for any residual client-side mitigations.

tomas: I'll open PR for autotune safety cap and add a perf test harness job that simulates mixed sequence-length traffic during canaries.

alex: Postmortem owners: alex (incident lead), tomas (investigation & fix), maya (customer comms). We'll schedule a follow-up rev on the runbook: add explicit per-tenant caps and shard-scoped canary checks to the autotune rollout steps.

support-linda: Noted. I'll close INC-4229 after confirmed with NimbusCorp.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=SEV3, status=mitigated, incident_id=INC-2026-0912. Follow-up tasks created: TASK-7781 (autotune cap), TASK-7782 (orchestrator rollout fix), TASK-7783 (runbook update).

alex: Thanks all. Keep an eye for regressions for the next 2 hours. If we get a repeat, escalate to SEV2 and consider hotpatch path. :thumbsup:

sre-ivy: Acknowledged. Monitoring window started.

(End of thread)
